		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 72pt;line-height:120%;text-indent: -72pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><a name="Item7MDA"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 7.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;MANAGEMENT&#x2019;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 72pt;line-height:120%;text-indent: -72pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Linear Technology Corporation, a member of the S&amp;P 500, has been designing, manufacturing and marketing a broad line of high performance analog integrated circuits for major companies worldwide for over three decades. The Company&#x2019;s products provide an essential bridge between our analog world and the digital electronics in communications, networking, industrial, automotive, computer, medical, instrumentation, consumer, and military and aerospace systems. Linear Technology produces power management, data conversion, signal conditioning, RF and interface ICs, &#xB5;Module</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:120%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;"> subsystems, and wireless sensor network products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Quarterly revenues of $379.5 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2015 increased $14.1 million or 3.8% over $365.4 million reported in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2014 and increased $7.5 million or</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2.0% over the previous quarter&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s revenue of $372.0 million. Net income of $132.7 million increased $3.0 million or 2.3% over the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2014 but decreased $2.5 million or 1.8% from the third quarter of fiscal year 2015. Diluted earnings per share of $0.54 per share in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2015 increased $0.01 per share or 2% over the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2014 but decreased $0.01 per share or 2% from the third quarter of fiscal year 2015. Net income and diluted earnings per share decreased on a sequential basis primarily due to a higher effective tax rate of 25.25% compared to 22.50% in the third quarter of fiscal 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Revenue for fiscal year 2015 was $1,475.1 million, an increase of</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$86.7 million </font><font style="display: inline;">or 6.2% </font><font style="display: inline;">over revenue of $1,388.4 million in the prior fiscal year. Net income of $521.0 million for fiscal year 2015 increased $61.0 million or 13.3% over $460.0 million reported in the previous fiscal year. Net income grew at a greater percentage than revenue primarily due to the extinguishment of the Convertible Senior Notes at the end of fiscal 2014. Accordingly, fiscal year 2015 had no related interest expense.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States, which require it to make estimates and judgments that significantly affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses and related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities. The Company regularly evaluates these estimates, including those related to inventory valuation, revenue recognition and income taxes. These estimates are based on historical experience and on assumptions that are believed by management to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results may differ from these estimates, which may impact the carrying values of assets and liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company believes the following critical accounting policies affect the more significant judgments and estimates used in the preparation of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes revenues when the earnings process is complete, when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, the product has been delivered, the price is fixed and determinable and collection is reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">During fiscal years 2015 and 2014, the Company recognized </font><font style="display: inline;">approximately 15% of net revenues from domestic distributors that are recognized under agreements which provide for certain sales price rebates and limited product return privileges</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Given the uncertainties associated with the levels of pricing rebates, the ultimate sales price on domestic distributor sales transactions is not fixed or determinable until domestic distributors sell the merchandise to the end-user.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the time of shipment to domestic distributors, the Company records a trade receivable and deferred revenue at the distributor purchasing price since there is a legally enforceable obligation from the distributor to pay for the products delivered.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company relieves inventory as title has passed to the distributor and recognizes deferred cost of sales in the same amount. &#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors&#x201D; represents the difference between deferred revenue and deferred cost of sales and is recognized as a current liability until such time as the </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">26</font>

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 8pt">

			<a href="#TableOfContents"><font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">distributor confirms a final sale to its end </font><font style="display: inline;">customer.&nbsp;&nbsp;At June 28, 2015, the Company had approximately $58.8 million of deferred revenue and $11.9 million of deferred cost of sales recognized as $46.9 million of &#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors.&#x201D;&nbsp;At June 29, 2014, the Company had approximately $56.8 million of deferred revenue and $11.2 million of deferred cost of sales recognized as $45.6 million of &#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;The</font><font style="display: inline;"> Company believes that its deferred costs of revenues have limited risk of material impairment, as the Company offers stock rotation privileg</font><font style="display: inline;">es to distributors (up to </font><font style="display: inline;">5% of quarterly purchases) which enable distributors to rotate slow moving inventory. In addition, stock rotated inventory that is returned to the Company is generally resalable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company reviews distributor ending on-hand inventory balances, as well as orders placed on the Company to ensure that distributors are not overstocking parts and are ordering to forecasted demand. To the extent the Company w</font><font style="display: inline;">as</font><font style="display: inline;"> to have a significant </font><font style="display: inline;">reduction in distributor price or grant significant price rebates, there could be a material impact on the ultimate revenue and gross profit recognized. </font><font style="display: inline;">During fiscal years 2015 and 2014, t</font><font style="display: inline;">he price rebates that have been remitted back to distributors have ranged from $3.5 million to $4.4 million per quarter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s sales to international distributors are made under agreements which permit limited stock return privileges but not sales price rebates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue on these sales is recognized upon shipment at which time title passes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has reserves to cover expected product returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;If product returns for a particular fiscal period exceed or are below expectations, the Company may determine that additional or less sales return allowances are required to properly reflect its estimated exposure for product returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, changes to sales return allowances have not had a significant impact on operating margin.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Inventory Valuation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company values inventories at the lower of cost or market.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company records charges to write-down inventories for unsalable, excess or obsolete raw materials, work-in-process and finished goods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Newly introduced parts are generally not valued until success in the market place has been determined by a consistent pattern of sales and backlog among other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company arrives at the estimate for newly released parts by analyzing sales and customer backlog against ending inventory on hand.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company reviews the assumptions on a quarterly basis and makes decisions with regard to inventory valuation based on the current business climate.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to write-downs based on newly introduced parts, judgmental assessments are calculated for the remaining inventory based on salability, obsolescence, historical experience and current business conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;If actual market conditions are less favorable than those projected by management, additional inventory write-downs may be required that could adversely affect operating results. If actual market conditions are more favorable, the Company may have higher gross margins when products are sold.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales to date of such products have not had a significant impact on gross margin.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company must make certain estimates and judgments in determining income tax expense for financial statement purposes. These estimates and judgments occur in the calculation of tax credits, tax benefits and deductions and in the calculation of certain tax assets and liabilities, which arise from differences in the timing of recognition of revenue and expense for tax and financial statement purposes. Significant changes to these estimates may result in an increase or decrease to the tax provision in a subsequent period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The calculation of the Company&#x2019;s tax liabilities involves uncertainties in the application of complex tax regulations. The Company recognizes liabilities for uncertain tax positions based on the two-step process prescribed in the authoritative accounting literature. The first step is to evaluate the tax position for recognition by determining if the weight of available evidence indicates that it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained on audit, including resolution of related appeals or litigation processes, if any. The second step requires the Company to estimate and measure the tax benefit as the largest amount that is more than 50% likely to be realized upon ultimate settlement. It is inherently difficult and subjective to estimate such amounts, as the Company has to determine the probability of various possible outcomes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company reevaluates these uncertain tax positions on a quarterly basis. This evaluation is based on factors including, but not limited to, changes in facts or circumstances, changes in tax law, effectively settled issues under audit, and new audit activity. Such a change in recognition or measurement would result in the recognition of a tax benefit or an additional charge to the tax provision. Refer to Note 11 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for a discussion of current tax matters.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Fiscal year 2015 revenues of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,475.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million increased $86.7 million or 6.2% over revenues of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,388.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal year </font><font style="display: inline;">2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fiscal year 2015 revenues increased over the prior fiscal year due to increases in revenues in </font><font style="display: inline;">all of the</font><font style="display: inline;"> end-markets </font><font style="display: inline;">led</font><font style="display: inline;"> by the </font><font style="display: inline;">Industrial and Automotive</font><font style="display: inline;"> end-market</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company continues to limit its exposure to the Consumer and cell-phone end-markets in favor of the Industrial, Automotive, Communication infrastructure and Military end-markets</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s bookings in the Industrial, Automotive, Communication infrastructure, and Military end-markets in aggregate were 88% of bookings in fiscal year 2015, as compared to 88% of bookings for fiscal year 2014 and 86% in fiscal 2013.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Factors Affecting Future Operating Results</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Except for historical information contained herein, the matters set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the statements in the following paragraphs, are forward-looking statements that are dependent on certain risks and uncertainties including such factors, among others, as the timing, volume and pricing of new orders received and shipped during a fiscal period, timely ramp-up of new facilities, the timely introduction of new processes and products; fluctuations in costs associated with utilities, transportation and raw materials; currency fluctuations; the effects of adverse economic and financial conditions in the United States and throughout the world; and other factors described below and in&nbsp;&#x201C;Item 1A &#x2013; Risk Factors&#x201D; section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Quarterly revenues of $379.5 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2015 increased $7.5 million or 2.0% over the previous quarter's revenue of $372.0 million.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> The Company&#x2019;s quarterly industry leading gross margin and operating margin percentages remained relatively steady at 76.1% and 46.5% while earnings per share declined $0.01 to $0.54 primarily due to a higher tax rate.&nbsp;For the fiscal year, revenue grew 6.2% to $1,475.1 million, while earnings per share increased 11.6% to $2.12. The fourth quarter is typically a strong quarter for the Company, although there were some concerns with global macroeconomic conditions that tempered expectations.&nbsp;As the quarter progressed, these conditions appeared to worsen and bookings slowed considerably.&nbsp;The bookings decline was broad based across all major markets and regions.&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s largest market, Industrial, suffered the largest decline followed by the Computer market which appears to be weak for the entire industry.&nbsp;In the early weeks of the first quarter of fiscal year 2016, bookings have improved.&nbsp;However, due to the decline in bookings received in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2015, coupled with a sluggish global economic environment, the Company is anticipating a difficult first fiscal quarter in fiscal year 2016.&nbsp;The Company forecasts revenue to decline sequentially in the 7% - 12% range. The Company is optimistic that this will be a short down cycle and that this is temporary weakness experienced as customers react to global uncertainties and adjust their inventories to match their cautiousness and end customer demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;Design activity remains robust and the Company sees many opportunities where new products may require our innovative analog solutions.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At June 28, 2015, cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $1,202.7 million, an increase of $189.9 million from the June 29, 2014 balance. Major uses of cash provided by operating activities of $598.9 million were (i)</font><font style="display: inline;"> cash dividends of $278.4 million, representing $1.14</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share for fiscal year 2015, (ii) $93.8 </font><font style="display: inline;">million to purchase 2.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million shares of the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s common stock in the open market and</font><font style="display: inline;">, (iii)</font><font style="display: inline;"> $30.4 million to purchase 0.7 million shares to satisfy minimum statutory withholding requirements related to the vesting of employee restricted stock awards.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#FF0000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Working capital at June 28, 2015 was $1,401.8 million.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s accounts receivable balance of $179.3 million at the end of fiscal year 2015 increased $5.9 million over the June 29, 2014 balance of $173.3 million. The increase is primarily due to higher shipments in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2015 as compared to the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Inventory totaled $99.9 million at the end of fiscal year 2015, an increase of $8.6 million over the prior year balance.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase in inventory was primarily du</font><font style="display: inline;">e to an increase in the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s work in process</font><font style="display: inline;"> inventory</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> primarily diebank, as well as in the</font><font style="display: inline;"> finished goods inventory</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company increased inventory levels for its newer products&nbsp;and increased its finished goods level to build up shippable inventory to meet anticipated sales.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s net property, plant and equipment balance of $287.7 at the end of fiscal year 2015 in</font><font style="display: inline;">creased $10.7 million over the prior year balance. Fixed </font><font style="display: inline;">asset additions totaled $62.6 million primarily </font><font style="display: inline;">for</font><font style="display: inline;"> procurement of assembly, test and wafer fabrication equipment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation expense was&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$51.9 million during fiscal year 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In July 2015, the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors declared a cash dividend of $0.30 per share.&nbsp;&nbsp;The $0.30 per share dividend will be paid on August 26, 2015 to stockholders of record on August 14, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The payment of future dividends will be based on financial performance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Historically, the Company has satisfied its liquidity needs through cash generated from operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Given its financial condition and historical operating performance, the Company believes that current capital resources and cash generated from operating activities should be sufficient to meet its liquidity and capital expenditures for the foreseeable future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On October 23, 2013, the Company entered into a $100.0 million credit agreement </font><font style="display: inline;">with </font><font style="display: inline;">Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (the &#x201C;Credit Agreement&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company </font><font style="display: inline;">originally </font><font style="display: inline;">entered into the Credit Agreement to enhance cash deployment flexibility in connection with the conversion of its Notes and potential</font><font style="display: inline;"> onshore cash requirements post-</font><font style="display: inline;">conversion.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">On July 27, 2015, the Credit Agreement was amended to increase the size of the line of credit to $150.0 million and to extend the maturity date from October 23, 2015 to July 27, 2017. The</font><font style="display: inline;"> Company has not utilized the Credit Agreement</font><font style="display: inline;"> to date</font><font style="display: inline;">. For further information on the </font><font style="display: inline;">Credit Agreement, see Note 7</font><font style="display: inline;"> of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<a name="Item7AQuantitativeAndQualitativeDisclosu"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">ITEM 7A.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Interest rate risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company&#x2019;s cash equivalents and marketable securities are subject to market risk, primarily interest rate and credit risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s investments are managed by outside professional managers within investment guidelines set by the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such guidelines include security type, credit quality and maturity and are intended to limit market risk by restricting the Company&#x2019;s investments to high quality </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">debt instruments with relatively short-term maturities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the weighted average duration of the Company&#x2019;s investments at June 28, 2015, a hypothetical 100 basis point increase in short-term interest rates would result in an unrealized loss in market value of the Company&#x2019;s investments totaling approximately $9.3 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;">Such losses would only be realized if the Company sold the investments prior to maturity. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> These investments are reported at fair</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> value with the related unrealized gains or losses reported in accumulated other comprehensive income, a component of stockholders&#x2019; deficit. The Company generally holds securities until maturity. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Foreign exchange risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company&#x2019;s sales outside the United States are transacted in U.S. dollars; accordingly, the Company&#x2019;s sales are not generally impacted by foreign currency rate changes. The operations outside of the United States incur operating expenses denominated in foreign currencies. The results of</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> operations and cash flows are therefore</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> subject to fluctuations due to changes in foreign currency exchange rates. The Company has not entered into any foreign currency exchange contracts to hedge foreign exchange risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Linear Technology Corporation (together with its consolidated subsidiaries, "Linear," &#x201C;Linear Technology&#x201D; or the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;), a member of the S&amp;P 500, has been designing, manufacturing and marketing a broad line of high performance analog integrated circuits for major companies worldwide for over three decades. The Company&#x2019;s products provide an essential bridge between our analog world and the digital electronics in communications, networking, industrial, automotive, computer, medical, instrumentation, consumer, and military and aerospace systems. Linear Technology produces power management, data conversion, signal conditioning, RF and interface ICs, &#xB5;Module</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:120%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;"> subsystems, and wireless sensor network products.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is a Delaware corporation; it was originally organized and incorporated in California in 1981.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Basis of Presentation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company operates on a 52/53-week fiscal year ending on the Sunday nearest June 30.&nbsp;Fiscal years </font><font style="display: inline;">2015, 2014 and 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> were 52-week years.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Fiscal year 2016 will be a 53-week fiscal year, with the additional week falling in the second quarter of fiscal year 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The accompanying consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries after elimination of all significant inter-company accounts and transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts denominated in foreign currencies have been remeasured using the U.S. dollar as the functional currency.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of financial statements and related disclosures in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States requires management to make estimates and judgments that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results could differ materially from those estimates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash equivalents are highly liquid investments purchased with original maturities of three months or less at the time of purchase.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cash equivalents consist of investment grade securities in commercial paper, bank certificates of deposit, and money market funds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Investments with maturities over three months at the time of purchase are classified as marketable securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;At </font><font style="display: inline;">June 28, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">June 29, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company&#x2019;s marketable securities balance consisted primarily of debt securities in municipal bonds, corporate bonds, commercial paper, U.S. and foreign government and agency securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s marketable securities are managed by outside professional managers within investment guidelines set by the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s investment guidelines generally restrict the professional managers to high quality debt instruments with a credit rating of AAA.&nbsp;&nbsp; Within the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s investment policy there is a provision that allows the Company to hold AA+ securities under certain circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s investments in debt securities are classified as available-for-sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;Investments in available-for-sale securities are reported at fair value with unrealized gains and losses, net of tax, as a component of &#x201C;Accumulated other comprehensive income&#x201D; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company classifies investments with maturities greater than twelve months as current as it considers all investments as a potential source of operating cash regardless of maturity date.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost of securities matured or sold is based on the specific identification method.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The allowance for doubtful accounts reflects the Company&#x2019;s best estimate of probable losses inherent in the accounts receivable balance. The Company determines the allowance based on the aging of its accounts receivable, historical experience, known troubled accounts, management judgment and other currently available evidence.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company writes off accounts receivable against the allowance when it determines a balance is uncollectible and no longer actively pursues collection of the receivable.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Concentrations of Credit Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s investment policy restricts investments to high credit quality investments with maturities of three years or less and limits the amount invested with any one issuer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Concentrations of credit risk with respect to accounts receivable are generally not significant due to the diversity of the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s customers, customer end-markets, and customer geographical locations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company performs ongoing credit evaluations of its customers</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;"> financial condition and requires collateral, primarily letters of credit, as deemed necessary.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Arrow Electronics In</font><font style="display: inline;">c</font><font style="display: inline;">. (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Arrow</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">), the Company&#x2019;s largest distributor, distributes the Company&#x2019;s products worldwide.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">Arrow is one of the largest distributors of electronic components in the world</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;">with revenues of $22.8 billion in their December 2014 fiscal year-end.&nbsp;&nbsp;Arrow&#x2019;s global components business segment covers the world&#x2019;s largest electronics markets - the Americas, EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa), and Asia Pacific regions.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">As of June 28, 2015 and June 29, 2014, Arrow worldwide accounted f</font><font style="display: inline;">or </font><font style="display: inline;">36%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">38%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the Company&#x2019;s total net accounts receivable, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Arrow worldwide accounted </font><font style="display: inline;">for </font><font style="display: inline;">32%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">31%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">31%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the Company&#x2019;s worldwide net revenues in fiscal 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Arrow, like the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> other distributors, is not an end customer, but rather serves as a channel of sale to many end users of the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s products.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">No end customer accounted for more than 10% of the Company&#x2019;s worldwide net revenues for any of the periods presented.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s assets, liabilities and cash flows are predominantly U.S. dollar denominated, including those of its foreign operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, the Company&#x2019;s foreign subsidiaries have certain assets, liabilities and cash flows that are subject to foreign currency risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the three years ended </font><font style="display: inline;">June 28, 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company did not utilize derivative instruments to hedge foreign currency risk or for any other purpose.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gains and losses resulting from foreign currency fluctuations are recognized in income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Inventories</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company values inventories at the lower of cost or market on a first-in, first-out basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company records charges to write-down inventories for unsalable, excess or obsolete raw materials, work-in-process and finished goods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Newly introduced parts are generally not valued until success in the market place has been determined by a consistent pattern of sales and backlog among other factors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to write-downs based on newly introduced parts, judgmental assessments are calculated for the remaining inventory based on salability, obsolescence, historical experience and current business conditions.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Property</font><font style="display: inline;">, plant and equipment is </font><font style="display: inline;">stated at cost and depreciated </font><font style="display: inline;">using t</font><font style="display: inline;">he straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets, which is generally </font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">-</font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> years for equipment and </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;">-</font><font style="display: inline;">30</font><font style="display: inline;"> years</font><font style="display: inline;"> for buildings</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of the asset&#x2019;s useful life or t</font><font style="display: inline;">he expected term of the lease.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Depreciation expense for fiscal years 2015, 2014, and 2013 was </font><font style="display: inline;">$51.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$49.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$49.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company reviews goodwill and purchased intangible assets with indefinite lives for impairment annually and whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of an asset may not be recoverable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reviews are performed to determine whether the carrying value of an asset is impaired, based on comparisons to undiscounted expected future cash flows. If this comparison indicates that there is impairment, the impaired asset is written down to fair value, which is typically calculated using: (i) quoted market prices or (ii) discounted expected future cash flows utilizing a discount rate consistent with the guidance. Impairment is based on the excess of the carrying amount over the fair value of those assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill is recorded as the difference, if any, between the aggregate consideration paid for an acquisition and the fair value of the net tangible and intangible assets acquired.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company tests goodwill for impairment at the reporting unit level (operating segment or one level below an operating segment) on an annual basis or more frequently if the Company believes indicators of impairment exist. During fiscal year 2015, the Company performed a qualitative assessment to test goodwill for impairment. Based on the qualitative assessment, if the Company determines that the fair value of a reporting unit is more likely than not (i.e.</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> a likelihood of more than 50 percent) to be less than its carrying amount, the two step impairment test will be performed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first step of the impairment test involves comparing the fair values of the applicable reporting units with their aggregate carrying values, including goodwill.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company generally determines the fair value of the Company&#x2019;s reporting units using the income approach methodology of valuation that includes the discounted cash flow method as well as other generally accepted valuation methodologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds the reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value, the Company performs the second step of the goodwill impairment test to determine the amount of impairment loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;The second step of the goodwill impairment test involves comparing the implied fair value of the affected reporting unit&#x2019;s goodwill with the carrying value of that goodwill.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> impairment charges were recor</font><font style="display: inline;">ded associated with the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s goodwill and intangible assets for any of the periods presented.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Advertising Expense</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company expenses advertising costs in the period in which they occur. Advertising expenses for fiscal years 2015, 2014, and 2013 were approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$5.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes revenues when the earnings process is complete, when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, the product has been delivered, the price is fixed and determinable and collection is reasonably assured.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognized approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">15%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of net revenues in fiscal year 2015 from North American (&#x201C;domestic&#x201D;) distributors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Domestic distributor revenues are recognized under agreements</font><font style="display: inline;"> which provide for certain sales price rebates and limited product return privileges.&nbsp;&nbsp;Given the uncertainties associated with the levels of pricing rebates, the ultimate sales price on domestic distributor sales transactions is not fixed or determinable until domestic distributors sell the merchandise to the end-customer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Domestic distributor agreements permit the following: price protection on certain domestic distribution inventory if the Company lowers the prices </font><font style="display: inline;">of its products; exchanges up to </font><font style="display: inline;">5%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of certain</font><font style="display: inline;"> purchases on a quarterly basis; and ship and debit transactions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Ship </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">and debit transactions occur when the Company agrees to accept a lower selling price for a specific quantity of product at the request of the domestic distributor in order to complete a sales transaction in the domestic distributor channel.&nbsp;&nbsp;For such sales, the Company rebates the negotiated price decrease to the distributor upon shipment as a reduction in the accounts receivable from the distributor.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 8pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At the time of shipment to domestic distributors, the Company records a trade receivable and deferred revenue at the distributor&#x2019;s purchase price since there is a legally enforceable obligation from the distributor to pay for the products delivered. The Company relieves inventory as title has passed to the distributor and recognizes deferred cost of sales in the same amount. &#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors&#x201D; represents the difference between deferred revenue and deferred costs of sales and is recognized as a current liability&nbsp;until such time as the distributor confirms a final sale to its end customer.&nbsp;&nbsp;&#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors&#x201D; effectively represents the deferred gross margin on the sale to the distributor, however, the actual amount of gross margin the Company ultimately recognizes in future periods may be less than the originally recorded amount as a result of price protection, negotiated price rebates and exchanges as mentioned above.&nbsp;&nbsp;The wide range and variability of negotiated price rebates granted to </font><font style="display: inline;">distributors does not allow the Company to accurately estimate the portion of the balance in the &#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors&#x201D; that will be remitted back to the distributors. </font><font style="display: inline;"> During fiscal years 2015 and 2014, t</font><font style="display: inline;">hese price rebates that have been remitted back to distributors have ranged from </font><font style="display: inline;">$3.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million to </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million per quarter.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> does not reduce deferred income by anticipated future price rebates. Instead, price rebates are recorded against &#x201C;Deferred income on shipments to distributors&#x201D; when incurred, which is generally at the time the distributor sells the product to the end customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s sales to international distributors are made under agreements which permit limited stock return privileges but not sales price rebates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The agreements generally permit distributors to exchange up to </font><font style="display: inline;">5%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of purchases on a semi-annual basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue on international distributor sales is recognized upon shipment at which time title passes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company estimates international distributor returns based on historical data and current business expectations and defers a portion of international distributor revenues and costs based on these estimated returns.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Product Warranty and Indemnification</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s warranty policy provides for the replacement of defective parts.&nbsp;&nbsp;In certain large contracts, the Company has agreed to negotiate in good faith a product warranty in the event that an epidemic failure of its parts was to take place. To date there have been no significant occurrences</font><font style="display: inline;"> of epidemic failure</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Warranty expense historically has been immaterial.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company provides a limited indemnification for certain customers against intellectual property infringemen</font><font style="display: inline;">t claims related to the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s products. In certain cases, there are limits o</font><font style="display: inline;">n and exceptions to the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s potential liability for indemnification relating to intellectual property infringement claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;To date, the Company has not incurred any significant indemnification expenses relating to intellectual property infringement claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company cannot estimate the amount of potential future payments, if any, which the Company might be required to make as a result of these agreements, and accordingly, the Company has not accrued any amounts for its indemnification obligations.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has equity incentive plans, which are described more fully in &#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Note 2: Stock-Based Compensation</font><font style="display: inline;">.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock-based compensation is measured at the grant date, based on the fair v</font><font style="display: inline;">alue of the award.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s equity awards granted in fiscal years 2015 and 2014 were restricted stock awards. Stock-based compensation cost for restricted stock awards is based on the fair market value of the Company&#x2019;s stock on the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock-based compensation cost for stock options is calculated on the date of grant using the fair value of stock options as determined using the Black-Scholes valuation model.&nbsp;The Black-Scholes valuation model requires the Company to estimate key assumptions such as expected option term and stock price volatility to determine the fair value of a stock option.&nbsp;&nbsp;The estimate of these key assumptions is based on historical information and judgment regarding market factors and trends.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company amortizes restricted stock and stock option award compensation cost straight-line over the awards vesting period, which is generally </font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes a tax benefit from an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained on examination by the taxing authorities, based on the technical merits of the position.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes liabilities for uncertain tax positions based on the two-step process prescribed in the authoritative accounting literature. The first step is to evaluate the tax position for recognition by determining if the weight of available evidence indicates that it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained on audit, including resolution of related appeals or litigation processes, if any. The second step requires the Company to estimate and measure the tax benefit as the largest amount that is more than 50% likely to be realized upon ultimate settlement.&nbsp;&nbsp;See &#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Note 11. Income Taxes</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; for further information.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Recently Announced Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the Financial Accounting Standard Board (&#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) No. 2014-09 Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606). On July 9, 2015, the FASB agreed to delay the effective date by one year from the first quarter of fiscal year 2018. In accordance with the agreed upon delay, the new standard is effective for us beginning in the first quarter of 2019. Early adoption is permitted, but not before the original effective date of the standard. The core principle of ASU No. 2014-09 is that a company should recognize revenue when it transfers promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU No. 2014-09 provides for one of the two methods of transition: retrospective application to each prior period presented; or recognition of the cumulative effect of retrospective application of the new standard in the period of initial application.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently evaluating the impact of ASU No. 2014-09 on its consolidated financial statements and which transition method to elect.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In August 2014, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-15, Disclosure of Uncertainties about an Entity&#x2019;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern. Each reporting period, management is required to assess whether there is substantial doubt about an entity&#x2019;s ability to continue as a going concern and if so to provide related footnote disclosures. The new guidance is effective for annual and interim periods ending after December&nbsp;15, 2016. Early adoption is permitted. This ASU is not expected to have an impact on the Company&#x2019;s financial statements or disclosures</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 3.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair Value</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has determined that the only assets</font><font style="display: inline;"> and liabilities in the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s financial statements that are required to be measured at fair value on a recurring basis are the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s investment portfolio assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Financial instruments are categorized in a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the information used to develop assumptions for measuring fair value and expands disclosures about fair value measurements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value hierarchy gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 input); then to quoted prices (in non-active markets or in active markets for similar assets or liabilities), inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, and inputs that are not directly observable, but that are corroborated by observable market data for the asset or liability (Level 2 input); then the lowest priority to unobservable i</font><font style="display: inline;">nputs, for example, the Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s data about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability (Level 3 input).&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is a market-based measurement, not an entity-specific measurement, and a fair value measurement should therefore be based on the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s Level 1 assets consist of investments in money-market funds and United States Treasury securities that are actively traded</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Arial;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s Level 2 assets consist of municipal bonds, obligations of U.S. government-sponsored enterprises, corporate debt and commercial paper that are less actively traded in the market, but where quoted market prices exist for similar instruments that are actively traded.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company determines the fair value of its Level 2 assets by obtaining non-binding market prices from its third-party portfolio managers on the last day of the quarter.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> Level 3 assets in fiscal years </font><font style="display: inline;">2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2014</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 5</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill and Intangible Assets</font>

			<font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:4pt;"></font><font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:4pt;text-align:left"><font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">On December&nbsp;20, 2011, the Company acquired </font><font style="display: inline;">100%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the outstanding stock of privately held Dust Networks ("Dust") of Hayward, California, a provider of low power wireless sensor network technology.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">As a result of the acquisition the Company recorded goodwill and intangible assets during fiscal year 2012.</font></font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Amortization expense associated with intangible assets for fiscal year 2015, 2014, and 2013 was </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$6.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Amortization expense for intangible assets is estimated to be </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal year 2016, </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal year 2017, </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal year 2018, </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal year 2019, </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal year 2020 and </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million thereafter.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Note 6.&nbsp;&nbsp;Convertible Senior Notes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2007, the Company issued </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> billion aggregate principal amount of Convertible Senior Notes (the &#x201C;Notes&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Notes paid cash interest ranging from </font><font style="display: inline;">3.00%</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">3.125%</font><font style="display: inline;"> semiannually.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company used the entire net proceeds of the offering to fund a portion of its repurchase of </font><font style="display: inline;">$3.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> billion of its common stock pursuant to an accelerated stock repurchase transaction.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In accordance with the provisions of ASC 470-20-10 to 35, the Company recognized an effective interest rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">5.69%</font><font style="display: inline;"> on the carrying value of the Notes. The difference between the effective interest rate of 5.69% and the Notes cash coupon rates of 3.00% to 3.125% resulted in non-cash interest expense from the amortization of debt discount representing the equity feature of the Notes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On May 1, 2014 the Company executed the conversion of the outstanding principal amount of the Notes totaling </font><font style="display: inline;">$845.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon the conversion price of </font><font style="display: inline;">$40.68</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share, each $1,000 principal amount of the Notes was converted at a rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">24.582</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the conversion, holders of the Notes received the principal amount of $845.1 million in cash and the remaining conversion premium was settled in shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock totaling approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">2.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million shares.&nbsp;&nbsp;There was </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> gain or loss recognized as a result of the conversion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have audite</font><font style="display: inline;">d Linear Technology Corporation&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting as of June 28, 2015 based on criteria established in Internal Control-Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria)</font><font style="display: inline;">. Linear Technology Corporation&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit. </font>
